raw_case_text:
A 34-year-old male with stage IV cirrhosis secondary to autoimmune hepatitis (AH) and concomitant alcoholism presented to a regional hospital emergency room with fever, vomiting, and altered mentation in the setting of presumed alcohol withdrawal. His prior diagnosis of AH was made two years' prior via transhepatic biopsy and treatment was initiated with azathioprine and prednisone; however, the patient was nonadherent. He immigrated from Pakistan in 2009 and was married with a 4-year-old daughter with no family history of autoimmunity.
At the initial assessment, the patient was hyperthermic at 41.5 C, tachycardic with a heart rate of 132 beats per minute, and tachypneic at 24 breaths per minute with normal oxygen saturation. Bedside examination revealed livedo reticularis of his lower extremities with palmar erythema and spider nevi. His abdomen was slightly firm with tenderness in his right upper quadrant. No organomegaly or peritoneal signs were identified.
Due to suspected sepsis and severe alcohol withdrawal, he was transferred to the ICU for intubation and agitation management. Additionally, broad-spectrum antimicrobial treatment was initiated with coverage for spontaneous bacterial peritonitis and presumed community-acquired meningitis with meropenem, vancomycin, and acyclovir. Over the coming four days, his level of consciousness continued to decline and he developed seizures.
Diagnostic workup revealed severe acute thrombocytopenia (9000/mm3) and neutropenia (1100/mm3) compared to normal values a week prior. Blood chemistry demonstrated a mixed cholestatic and hepatocellular enzyme elevation. Over four days, AST values increased rapidly to 2388 IU/L with worsening direct hyperbilirubinemia (40 mcg-mol/L). Synthetic function demonstrated an INR of 1.2, normal glucose and hypoalbuminemia (25g/L). CT imaging of the chest, abdomen and pelvis showed enlargement of the spleen with evidence of hepatic cirrhosis. Ferritin levels were significantly elevated at greater than 8000 mcg/L with an elevated triglyceride level at 10.35 mmol/L. Bone marrow biopsy showed hemophagocytosis and increased macrophage infiltration (see Figure 1).
Infectious workup included extensive blood and urine testing for Hepatitis A, B, C, HIV, herpes simplex, varicella, cytomegalovirus (CMV), Epstein Barr Virus (EBV), acid-fast bacilli, and respiratory viruses. Bone marrow testing for leishmaniasis was negative. Rheumatologic workup yielded a >1:640 speckled ANA pattern, with positive beta-2 microglobulin and lupus type inhibitors present. Extensive workup demonstrated normal C3/4, dsDNA, anti-cardiolipin antibodies, MPO/PR3, anti-smith, AMA, ANCAs, anti-GBM, and HLA phenotyping were all normal. Toxic alcohol screen was similarly negative. Repeat transhepatic biopsy demonstrated known cirrhosis and no evidence of on-going AH. Finally, evaluation for malignancy including enhanced body CT imaging, serum flow cytometry, and immunoglobulins were all normal.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 34-year-old Pakistani-born male with stage IV autoimmune hepatitis cirrhosis and alcohol use disorder presented to the emergency department with hyperthermia (41.5 C), vomiting, and altered mental status.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient presented with high fever, vomiting, agitation, and altered mentation initially attributed to alcohol withdrawal and sepsis. Despite ICU intubation and broad-spectrum antimicrobial coverage (meropenem, vancomycin, and acyclovir), he developed progressive coma, seizures, fulminant cytopenias, and severe transaminitis over 4 days.
subjective.past_medical_history: Stage IV hepatic cirrhosis secondary to biopsy-proven autoimmune hepatitis (diagnosed 2 years prior; nonadherent to prescribed azathioprine and prednisone) and concomitant alcoholism; immigrated from Pakistan in 2009; no family history of autoimmune disease.
subjective.review_of_systems: Nonadherent to prescribed azathioprine and prednisone; positive for fever, vomiting, agitation, coma, and seizures.

objective.physical_examination: Temperature 41.5 C, HR 132 bpm, RR 24 breaths/min, normal SpO2; altered mental status progressing to coma and seizures; lower-extremity livedo reticularis, palmar erythema, and spider nevi; slightly firm abdomen with right upper quadrant tenderness and no palpable organomegaly or peritonism.
objective.routine_investigations: Labs over 4 days showed acute severe thrombocytopenia (9,000/mm3) and neutropenia (1,100/mm3), AST rising rapidly to 2,388 IU/L, direct bilirubin 40 umol/L, INR 1.2, albumin 25 g/L, normal glucose, ferritin >8,000 ug/L, triglycerides 10.35 mmol/L, speckled ANA >1:640, elevated beta-2 microglobulin, and positive lupus-type inhibitor, with normal C3/C4, anti-dsDNA, anticardiolipin, MPO/PR3 ANCA, anti-Sm, AMA, anti-GBM, immunoglobulins, and toxic alcohol screen. Extensive blood and urine testing for HAV, HBV, HCV, HIV, HSV, VZV, CMV, EBV, AFB, and respiratory viruses was negative.
objective.advanced_workup: Chest, abdominal, and pelvic CT showed hepatic cirrhosis and splenomegaly without malignancy. Repeat transhepatic liver biopsy showed established cirrhosis without active autoimmune hepatitis. Bone marrow biopsy demonstrated increased macrophage infiltration and prominent hemophagocytosis, with negative bone marrow testing for Leishmania.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Visceral leishmaniasis, viral/bacterial sepsis, active autoimmune hepatitis flare, and malignancy were excluded; fulfilment of HLH criteria (fever 41.5 C, splenomegaly, bicytopenia, ferritin >8,000 ug/L, triglycerides 10.35 mmol/L, and bone marrow hemophagocytosis) confirmed secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) in a patient with autoimmune hepatitis cirrhosis.
